title: Salzbackerln Nockerl (Salt-Baked Noodles)
description: Prepared with salt, milk or cream, and butter or fat.
steps: In a deep bowl, combine 1 liter flour, 1 tablespoon salt, and 2 whole eggs
Stir with as much milk or cream as needed to make a smooth, pourable dough
Beat the dough until it falls from the spoon
Place dough on a board and strip pieces of desired size into boiling salted water using a knife kept in hot water
Cover and poach for 10-15 minutes
Pour into a colander, rinse with cold water, place in a pot containing 16 hectograms hot butter or fat, stir well, and use as a garnish when hot

title: Salzburger Nockerl (Salzburg Dumplings)
description: Prepared with milk or cream, egg yolks, and powdered sugar.
steps: Prepare a standard butter dough from 1/4 liter flour
Fill this dough into a pastry bag with a tube opening (not star-shaped)
3/4 hour before serving, bring 1 liter milk or cream to a boil in a casserole
Apply gentle pressure to the pastry bag so the dough comes out of the tube, cutting it into pieces of desired size with a knife into the boiling milk
Let the dumplings boil covered, shaking the casserole frequently
Meanwhile, beat 4 egg yolks with 3/4 liter cold milk or cream and 12 tablespoons powdered sugar
Pour this mixture into the casserole with the dumplings, stir together, and place in the oven for several minutes
When the milk has cooked down sufficiently, arrange the dumplings on a platter, sprinkle with sugar, and serve

title: Sauerfraut mit Ragout (Sauerkraut with Ragout)
description: Prepared with sauerkraut, broth, and fat.

ingredients.name: a little lemon juice if necessary

steps: Cook 1 heaping plate of sauerkraut with approximately 1 liter fatty broth and approximately 10 tablespoons fat gently in a covered pot

Let 2 crushed shallots or 1 piece garlic with 1 teaspoon finely cut green parsley roast in 8 tablespoons fat, add 2 tablespoons flour to it, pour it with 1/4 liter white wine and let it cook well

title: Sautéed Pheasant Breast Fillets (Filets de faisan sauté)
description: Prepared with pheasant, butter, and salt.
steps: After plucking and singeing the pheasant, cut the skin back at the neck, remove the crop and esophagus with a cloth, and lift away the skin over the breast
Make an incision at the top just below the wings
Carefully detach the breast on each side from the breastbone and skeleton
Carefully remove the strong sinew connecting the two parts without damaging the underbreasts
Smooth the underbreasts with a knife and place on a plate
From the large breasts, remove the fine skin attached with a knife and smooth these as well
Salt both large and underbreasts, place side by side in a casserole, cover with a paper sheet buttered and shaped to fit the casserole, and set aside

Draw out the dough finely, brush it with melted butter
Beat 2 whole eggs in half seidel milk cream well together, pour this over the dough

title: Schlehenwein (Sloe Wine)

title: Schnellräucherung ohne Feuer und Rauch (Quick-Smoking Without Fire and Smoke)
description: Prepared with meat, veal, and water or salt.

ingredients.name: All meat must be completely fresh
For veal: saltpeter, cooking salt, crushed juniper berries, chopped garlic, rose geranium leaves, lemon peel with white pith, bay leaves
Rain water or boiled well water
For the smoking process: 2 pounds gloss soot (chimney soot) from a chimney where only wood is burned, 6 measures (18 apothecary pounds) rain or boiled well water, 8 pounds cooking salt
For finishing: pure distilled wood vinegar

steps: Ensure all meat is completely fresh; for veal, remove from hide immediately after slaughtering to prevent unpleasant odors
Wash the veal meat clean and rub it with some saltpeter, then let it lie for four hours in a cool place in an appropriate oak or stone vessel without pressure
Dissolve cooking salt in warm rain water or boiled well water
Rub the meat firmly with crushed juniper berries, sprinkle with finely chopped garlic and some rose geranium leaves, lemon peels with white pith, and bay leaves
Ensure the meat forms no hollow spaces in its layers; fill any gaps with small pieces of the same meat to enable even pressure
Cover the meat with the cooled salt brine and let it stand for three days in a dry cellar, covered only with a cloth to protect from dirt, without any pressure
On the fourth day, load the meat with stones and increase pressure in winter until the twelfth day, then remove the stones; after two days, apply the previous pressure again for four days
For veal, the proper time in brine is eight to twelve days in summer, fourteen to eighteen days in winter
For beef and pork, use 14 pounds salt and 2 pounds saltpeter per 25 pounds meat; let it lie 24 days in winter or 14-18 days in summer
For poultry and fish, rub salt in the cavity (and some pepper may be used) but do not apply pressure
Approximately 60 hours before removing the meat from the salt brine, prepare 2 pounds of clean gloss soot by grinding it to fine powder
Pour 6 measures (18 apothecary pounds) of rain or boiled well water over the soot, cover the vessel, and stir the prepared brine frequently
Before the last two hours pass, add eight pounds of cooking salt to this soot brine and stir well
Remove the meat from the salt brine, let it drain, place it in another clean vessel, and cover it with the soot brine
If the brine is insufficient, mix the remaining sediment with the required amount of boiled water and add it
Let the treated meat lie for 5 to 6 hours depending on its diameter, tilting the vessel frequently
Remove the meat from the soot brine and hang it in an airy place, avoiding contact with walls, to dry completely
Finally, brush it with a brush using pure distilled, clarified wood vinegar (though it can be used immediately without this step)
Note that the meat must not remain too long in the gloss soot brine, as it would otherwise acquire an unpleasant pitch odor

For beef and pork, prepare the gloss soot brine from 6 pounds cooking salt, 1 pound pure gloss soot, and 5 measures water; weight these meats with stones and let them lie 8 to 9 hours, frequently turning the pieces and stirring the brine well
Poultry and fish remain in the veal's gloss soot brine for 1 to 2 hours depending on their size
All meat pieces must have loops attached before salting for later hanging and drying

All types of sausages made from fresh meat and fat of completely healthy animals, without excessive thinning of the sausage mass by meat broth or other liquids promoting souring, can be smoked without prior salting by lying 3 hours in the described gloss soot brine in a manner completely harmless to health; they should hang in the air at least 48 hours

title: Schokoladeis (Chocolate Glaze)

description: Prepared with batter, whipped cream, and strawberries or vanilla or sugar or marmalade or chocolate.

ingredients.name: 1 coffee cup fresh strawberries or 12 deca vanilla sugar, or any marmalade, or 2 bars grated chocolate

steps: Stir 14 deca finely pounded sugar and 3 whole eggs for 1 hour and after this time mix well with 10 deca flour.

On a baking sheet coated with wax and completely cooled, place 1/2 tablespoon of the above batter at 2 hand-widths distance apart, which you stretch with the spoon back-of-knife thickness lengthwise. Place the sheet in the oven and let it bake at moderate heat until the batter releases from the sheet; then remove the baking sheet from the oven, place it on the warm stove where you hold one end of the baked batter strip at the pointed end of the Sfarmitsche form, turn the batter obliquely over the form so that it forms a cone and then place it on a strainer.

Repeat this procedure with a second Sfarmitsche form, which is then also placed on the sheet, whereupon you remove the first twisted Sfarmitsche from the form, place it on a sieve and let it cool. Continue in this way until the batter is used up.

Then beat 1/4 liter whipped cream to thick foam, mix lightly with 16 deca sugar and 1 coffee cup fresh strawberries or 12 deca vanilla sugar, or any marmalade, or also with 2 bars grated chocolate and fill the cold Sfarmitschen with this. title: Ster-Krapfen (Star Fritters)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, sour cream, and flour.
steps: Put 32 deka flour on a strudel board, cut 12 deka butter into it, and work this with the flour

Work this into a dough until blisters become visible, then let it rest for an hour in a cool place

title: Strasbourg Pâté (Strasburger Pâté in Terrrine)
description: Prepared with duck or goose, bacon, and onions.

ingredients.name: 1 handful of finely cut yellow roasted onions

steps: Cut out the hearts, veins, and bloody fibers from 4 duck livers.
Round them by cutting the edges, place the livers in cold water, remove after 10 minutes, and lay on a cloth to dry.
Make 3 cuts on the curved side of each liver lengthwise.
Rub with pâté seasoning and place finely cut truffles into the cuts.
Pound the scraps from the livers with 1/2 kilo diced bacon in a mortar and pass with 1 handful of finely cut yellow roasted onions through a sieve into a bowl.
Mix well with 2 tablespoons rum and pâté seasoning.
Line a pâté terrine with 1 duck liver, add a spoonful of the prepared forcemeat, alternate livers and forcemeat until the terrine is full.
Cover with a fitting lid and seal.
Cook in a bain-marie for 1 hour for smaller terrines or up to 3.5 hours for larger ones.
Remove from heat, take off the lid, and let the pâté cool in the bain-marie.
Press the cooked mass firmly, turn out the terrine so all liquid drains well, and smooth it.
Pour cold clarified lard with ham over the pâté in the terrine high enough so the fat reaches to the outer edge.

title: Striekel (Braided Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with yeast, melted butter, and flour.

ingredients.name: 3 deca compressed yeast dissolved in 1/8 liter lukewarm milk

steps: Put 1 1/2 liter flour in a bowl, make a well in the middle, pour in 3 deca compressed yeast dissolved in 1/8 liter lukewarm milk
Stir it a little, dust with some flour and let it rise covered in a warm place
When this so-called sponge has risen, add 1 whole egg, 3/8 liter milk with 9 to 12 deca melted butter, 6 deca sugar and 1 teaspoon of salt
Stir it into a dough and knead it with the hands until it pulls away from them
Cover it in the bowl with a cloth and place in a warm location
After the dough has risen to double height, shape it into a striekel by placing the dough on a flour-dusted board and dividing it into 4 unequal pieces
Cut the largest piece into 4 pieces, shape these into 2 finger-thick ropes, which are then braided into a four-strand braid and gently stretched lengthwise
From the two next smaller pieces, by cutting each into 3 parts, make two 3-strand braids in the same way and stretch them slightly
Twist the remaining fourth piece into two ropes and twist them together lightly

Line a baking sheet with white writing paper, arrange the 4 braids in correct order (the four-strand at the bottom, the two-strand at the top) into a striekel shape and cover it with a cloth, let it rise 1/2 hour in a warm place
Brush the striekel with beaten egg and bake slowly for 1 hour in the oven

Alternatively, the dough can be shaped into a loaf placed in a floured breadmaking basket covered and placed in a warm location until it has risen to double height, then placed on a buttered baking sheet and treated as with the striekel
If desired, 1/8 deca raisins can be added when combining the dough for either the striekel or the loaf

title: Suppe Julienne (Julienne Soup)
description: A soup made with beef broth, partridge or woodcock, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: well-plucked and cleaned partridge or woodcock

steps: Make a particularly strong broth and cook it well, then clean it of all fat.
Strain it through a cloth, add necessary salt, and keep it hot.
Take a well-plucked and cleaned partridge or woodcock and pound it very finely raw in a mortar, removing the entrails from the partridge but not from the woodcock.
Add one serving spoon of broth and 4 egg yolks to it.
Pound everything together well, then strain it through a hair cloth.
If the strained mixture is too thick, add some cooled broth.
When the soup is hot and seasoned with salt and grated nutmeg to taste, pour it into the soup pot and add the strained mixture while constantly stirring.
